AMZN.rationale: Amazon presents a solid fundamental case with strong trajectory. Q3 2025 showed accelerating revenue ($180.2B, +7.4% QoQ) and EPS growth ($1.95, +16.1% QoQ), with three consecutive quarters of improvement. The business has excellent competitive positioning: AWS dominates cloud with ~29% market share and is reaccelerating (28% YoY growth in Q1 2026 per news), advertising is a $70B+ high-margin business growing 24% YoY, and the third-party marketplace generates $172B in fees with minimal inventory risk. Balance sheet is healthy with debt-to-equity of 0.149 and $369.6B equity. Operating cash flow is strong at $35.5B quarterly. However, the massive $200B 2026 capex commitment has collapsed trailing free cash flow to $1.2B, creating real near-term cash flow pressure. Valuation at P/E 36x is mid-range of its 28-39x 12-month window, neither cheap nor expensive versus own history. The stock has rallied 15.9% in the past quarter, partially reflecting the strong Q1 2026 earnings beat ($2.78 EPS vs $1.63 consensus). Key risks include the October 2026 FTC antitrust trial, EU regulatory pressure on AWS, and the question of whether $200B in AI capex will generate adequate returns. Multiple billionaire investors (Ackman, Tepper, Robbins) are buying while Berkshire exited. The Snowflake $6B AWS deal and Anthropic partnership provide near-term validation of AWS's AI positioning. News sentiment is moderately positive (mean 0.35). The score reflects strong fundamentals and trajectory offset by mid-range valuation and significant capex/cash flow uncertainty.
